overview: Créez des vidéos de 4 à 30 secondes à 24 FPS, du 480p à la 4K. Partez de texte ou d’images, guidez le résultat avec des références multimodales, ou utilisez Modify et Extend. Les sorties 1080p et 4K sont en HEVC 10 bits ; les résolutions proposées dépendent du parcours.

tips.title: Comment diriger une scène Seedance 2.5 plus longue
items: Écrivez un arc clair avec un début, une transition et une fin.
Associez un mouvement de caméra à chaque temps au lieu d’empiler les consignes.
Décrivez les causes et réactions visibles pour garder une physique lisible.
Gardez les dialogues brefs et reliez chaque réplique à une action ou une expression précise.

faqs.a: Seedance 2.5 crée des vidéos de 4 à 30 secondes à partir de texte, d’images ou de références combinées, avec un son généré en option. Importez un clip dans Modify pour retoucher un plan ou dans Extend pour poursuivre l’action.

faqs.q: Quelle est la durée des scènes présentées ?
faqs.a: La comédie pop de la section Create dure 30 secondes ; Hard Bounce dans le guide de prompt dure 24 secondes. Seedance 2.5 prend en charge des clips de 4 à 30 secondes et chaque exemple conserve sa résolution de sortie réelle.

faqs.q: Comment écrire le prompt d’une scène plus longue ?
faqs.a: Définissez d’abord le concept, associez les actions et la caméra à des temps précis, puis indiquez les contraintes de continuité et de sécurité à préserver.

faqs.q: Où utiliser Seedance 2.5 et consulter son tarif ?
faqs.a: Seedance 2.5 est accessible aux utilisateurs de MaxVideoAI dans Create. Choisissez la durée, la résolution et les références pour obtenir le prix affiché avant chaque rendu. Le Draft natif en 480p et sa finalisation sont facturés séparément.

faqs.q: Comment fonctionne le Draft natif de Seedance 2.5 ?
faqs.a: Générez un Draft natif en 480p pour vérifier mouvement et composition. Gardez la prise, puis choisissez un final 1080p ou 4K depuis ce Draft terminé. Draft et final sont deux générations avec leurs propres devis. Le final conserve le prompt, la durée, le cadrage, le son et les références du Draft. Ce parcours couvre texte, images, références, Modify et Extend ; un rendu 480p ordinaire n’est pas un Draft natif.

faqs.q: Seedance 2.5 peut-il générer une vidéo en 4K ?
faqs.a: Oui. Générez directement en 4K à partir de texte, d’images ou de références, ou finalisez un Draft natif en 4K. En 16:9, la 4K correspond à 3840 × 2160 ; les autres formats ont leurs propres dimensions. Les sorties 1080p et 4K sont en HEVC 10 bits. La résolution de retouche dépend du parcours : Modify standard propose le 480p/720p, tandis qu’un Draft natif Modify peut être finalisé en 1080p ou en 4K.

faqs.q: Quand choisir Seedance 2.5 plutôt que Flash ?
faqs.a: Choisissez Seedance 2.5 pour une livraison 1080p ou 4K, le parcours Draft natif vers final et un plus grand nombre de références. Flash convient au 480p/720p avec ses propres limites de références ; il ne propose pas la finalisation de Draft natif. Comparez le devis actuel avec les entrées et les réglages de votre projet.

section.title: Comment prompter Seedance 2.5
section.intro: Partez de l’idée qui relie la séquence. Pour un récit, ce peut être un personnage ou un objectif ; pour un clip musical, une forme, un mouvement ou un son. Décrivez ce qui relie les plans, puis donnez aux moments importants leur propre durée.
section.tip: Les durées servent le rythme et les accents. Explicitez le lien visuel entre les plans ; un découpage détaillé reste une direction à vérifier, pas une garantie de coupes à l’image près.

tabs.label: Concept
tabs.title: Définir l’arc de la scène
tabs.description: Précisez les personnages, le changement narratif et la destination finale de la scène.
tabs.copy:
Sujet et décor :
[Qui apparaît, où et avec quels détails visuels distinctifs]

Changement narratif :
[Ce qui évolue entre l’ouverture et le dernier temps]

Plan final :
[L’action, l’expression ou la composition finale]

Langage visuel :
[Lumière, palette, texture et caractère de l’objectif]

tabs.label: Chronologie
tabs.title: Diriger les temps du récit
tabs.description: Répartissez les actions et les mouvements de caméra sur toute la durée.
tabs.copy:
0 à 6 secondes :
[Composition d’ouverture + première action + mouvement de caméra]

6 à 14 secondes :
[Développement + réaction + transition de caméra]

14 à 22 secondes :
[Révélation principale ou temps de jeu + cadrage]

22 à 30 secondes :
[Résolution + position finale de la caméra]

Direction audio :
[Ambiance, dialogue bref et sons liés aux actions]

tabs.label: Contraintes
tabs.title: Protéger la continuité et la lisibilité
tabs.description: Indiquez les éléments qui ne doivent pas dériver pendant le développement de la scène.
tabs.copy:
Repères de continuité :
[Tenue, accessoires, lieu, lumière et direction à l’écran]

Règles physiques :
[Contact, poids, vitesse et réactions de l’environnement]

Règles de jeu :
[Regards, gestes, expression du visage et rythme du dialogue]

À éviter :
[Coupes indésirables, sujets dupliqués, changements brusques de caméra et artefacts visuels]

tabNotes.body: Le concept fixe un seul changement narratif lisible pour toute la scène.
La chronologie attribue une action et un mouvement de caméra à chaque temps.
Les contraintes répètent uniquement les détails qui doivent rester stables.

globalPrinciples: Choisissez une idée commune : un récit, un motif visuel récurrent ou un rythme physique.
Utilisez des plages temporelles pour ordonner les actions au lieu de tout demander en même temps.
Gardez un langage de caméra précis et physiquement compatible avec la scène.
Reliez les gestes, les expressions et les dialogues brefs aux temps visibles du récit.
engineWhy: La planification d’une scène plus longue donne assez de place à la mise en place, au développement et à la conclusion.
La direction minutée facilite l’évaluation de la caméra et du jeu, temps par temps.
Des règles physiques explicites aident à préserver des mouvements et des réactions crédibles dans toute la séquence.

demo.title: Hard Bounce — diriger un montage rythmé
demo.promptLabel: Prompt original du clip musical multi-plans
demo.prompt:
Create a 24-second ultra-stylized experimental underground music film.

TITLE / CONCEPT:
HARD BOUNCE

One fluorescent orange ball drives the entire edit.

Every impact, bounce, spin or circular motion creates the next shot.

The film becomes progressively faster, stranger and more visually aggressive.

The ORANGE CIRCLE is the recurring graphic motif:
basketball,
wheel,
vinyl record,
speaker,
washing-machine window,
human eye,
tunnel light,
moon,
then basketball again.

Every transition must be visually motivated by:
SHAPE,
MOTION,
DIRECTION,
or IMPACT.

This is NOT a story.
This is visual rhythm.

Dark, raw, underground, tactile, energetic.
Photorealistic but highly art-directed.

No text.
No logos.
No subtitles.

--------------------------------
SHOT 1 — 0:00–0:02
--------------------------------

TOTAL BLACK.

A fluorescent orange basketball drops from above into a single hard spotlight.

Concrete floor.

BOOM.

One massive dry impact.

On the first bounce, camera drops violently with the ball.

Second bounce:

BOOM.

HARD CUT EXACTLY ON IMPACT.

--------------------------------
SHOT 2 — 0:02–0:04
--------------------------------

Nighttime underground basketball court.

Wet black asphalt.
Chain-link fencing.
Sodium-vapor lights.
Steam in the distance.

EXTREME LOW FISHEYE CAMERA only centimeters above the floor.

A player in black sneakers dribbles the orange ball directly toward camera.

BOOM.
BOOM.
BOOM.

Each bounce becomes part of the beat.

On the final bounce, the ball completely fills frame.

MATCH CUT.

--------------------------------
SHOT 3 — 0:04–0:05.7
--------------------------------

The orange circle becomes the glowing hub of a motorcycle wheel.

Camera mounted inches beside the spinning wheel.

The motorcycle races through a wet concrete tunnel.

Reflections streak across the road.

Extreme speed.
Strong parallax.
Realistic vibration.

The wheel spins faster.

MATCH CUT ON ROTATION.

--------------------------------
SHOT 4 — 0:05.7–0:07.3
--------------------------------

A BLACK VINYL RECORD spins at exactly the same speed.

Orange center label.

Extreme macro.

Needle violently drops.

CRACK.

Bass enters.

Rapid macro details:
grooves,
dust,
needle vibration,
chrome reflections.

Camera dives INTO the spinning grooves.

--------------------------------
SHOT 5 — 0:07.3–0:09
--------------------------------

The vinyl grooves become curved concrete lines inside a brutalist skate bowl.

A skateboarder drops in at extreme speed.

Wide fisheye lens.

Camera races backward directly in front of the skateboard.

Wheels scream across concrete.

Skater launches over camera.

The underside of the board wipes the entire frame.

WHIP TRANSITION.

--------------------------------
SHOT 6 — 0:09–0:10.7
--------------------------------

Underground rave.

Almost total darkness.

Hard white strobe.

Bodies appear only for fractions of a second.

Sweat.
Chrome jewelry.
Black clothing.
Condensation.
Hands in the air.

In the center:

a giant circular orange speaker cone pulses.

Every bass hit physically moves the cone.

PUSH IN violently on the speaker.

BOOM.

BOOM.

BOOM.

On the third hit—

camera passes through it.

--------------------------------
SHOT 7 — 0:10.7–0:12.3
--------------------------------

Inside a fluorescent laundromat at 2AM.

Perfect symmetrical composition.

Rows of washing machines.

All machine windows are black...

except ONE glowing orange circular door.

Camera crash-zooms toward it.

Inside, orange fabric spins violently.

SPINNING MOTION MATCH CUT.

--------------------------------
SHOT 8 — 0:12.3–0:14
--------------------------------

EXTREME MACRO HUMAN EYE.

The orange washing-machine circle becomes a vivid amber iris.

Natural skin.
Tiny eyelashes.
Wet eye reflections.

The pupil rapidly contracts.

Reflected inside the pupil:

a subway train approaches.

Camera pushes directly through the pupil.

--------------------------------
SHOT 9 — 0:14–0:16
--------------------------------

SUBWAY PLATFORM.

Train blasts past camera at enormous speed.

Handheld.
Harsh fluorescent light.
Wind hits clothing and newspapers.

Very fast cuts:

train wheel —
shoe hitting platform —
door slamming —
hand grabbing metal rail —
orange emergency light —
eyes —
moving tunnel lights.

Each shot lasts only fractions of a second.

CLACK.
CLACK.
CLACK.
CLACK.

The rhythm accelerates.

--------------------------------
SHOT 10 — 0:16–0:18
--------------------------------

CAMERA IS NOW ATTACHED TO THE FRONT OF THE TRAIN.

We rocket through a black subway tunnel.

Circular tunnel lights flash directly toward camera.

Each light appears for one frame:

WHITE.
BLACK.
ORANGE.
BLACK.
WHITE.
BLACK.

Speed increases impossibly.

Then the final tunnel light becomes enormous.

MATCH CUT.

--------------------------------
SHOT 11 — 0:18–0:20
--------------------------------

The circle is now the FULL MOON.

Huge orange moon above brutalist apartment towers.

Camera drops vertically from the moon toward the city at extreme speed.

Down past rooftops,
balconies,
neon,
fire escapes,
streetlights.

FPV dive.

At street level—

someone throws the orange basketball upward directly toward camera.

--------------------------------
SHOT 12 — 0:20–0:22
--------------------------------

BALL FLIES PAST CAMERA.

ULTRA-FAST RHYTHMIC MONTAGE.

0.2–0.4 second fragments:

basketball bounce

motorcycle wheel

vinyl needle

skateboard landing

speaker pumping

washing machine spinning

eye blinking

subway wheel

tunnel light

moon

ball

Every circular image perfectly aligned in the center of frame.

Faster.

Faster.

Faster.

The soundtrack becomes a brutal synchronized audiovisual crescendo.

--------------------------------
SHOT 13 — 0:22–0:24
--------------------------------

Suddenly:

SILENCE.

Back to the exact dark concrete room from the opening.

The fluorescent orange ball drops into frame.

But this time—

a hand catches it ONE CENTIMETER before it hits the ground.

No impact.

Absolute silence.

Hold.

The fingers slowly release the ball.

It begins falling again.

CUT TO BLACK

one frame BEFORE impact.

BOOM.

END.

--------------------------------

AUDIO DESIGN:

Build an original underground electronic track entirely around PHYSICAL IMPACT.

The basketball bounce is the kick drum.

Motorcycle vibration becomes bass texture.

Vinyl crackle becomes high-frequency percussion.

Skateboard wheels become rhythmic noise.

Speaker cone becomes sub-bass.

Subway wheels become industrial percussion.

Train-door impacts become snares.

Tunnel lights introduce sharp electronic pulses.

The track must progressively accelerate from minimal rhythm into an aggressive experimental club beat.

Every important edit must land precisely on sound.

Use aggressive stereo movement during fast camera passages.

At 22 seconds:
REMOVE EVERYTHING.

Absolute silence.

Final BOOM occurs only after picture cuts to black.

--------------------------------

CAMERA LANGUAGE:

extreme fisheye
macro cinematography
camera mounted to moving objects
FPV flight
crash zooms
whip pans
snap zooms
rapid tracking
extreme low angles
Dutch camera rolls
hard handheld
speed ramps
one-frame inserts
perfect graphic match cuts

Avoid generic slow floating AI camera movement.

Camera movement should feel physical, dangerous and intentional.

--------------------------------

VISUAL LANGUAGE:

underground editorial cinema
brutalist architecture
late-night city culture
wet concrete
black asphalt
steel
chrome
sweat
steam
fluorescent practical lights
hard flash photography
16mm texture mixed with sharp modern digital cinematography
deep blacks
controlled highlights
strong grain
dirty lens moments
realistic motion blur

PALETTE:
almost monochrome world,
black,
concrete gray,
cold white,
dirty metallic tones.

FLUORESCENT ORANGE is the only strong recurring color.

Keep orange visually dominant only in the circular motif.

--------------------------------

EDITING RULE:

The audience should constantly anticipate the next impact.

BOUNCE = CUT.
ROTATION = MATCH CUT.
CIRCLE = NEW WORLD.
IMPACT = MUSIC.

Do not create random beautiful shots.

Every shot must visually or rhythmically connect to the previous one.

The video should feel edited by an exceptional human music-video editor:
fast,
precise,
dirty,
cool,
graphic,
unpredictable.

Avoid generic cyberpunk.
Avoid glossy sci-fi.
Avoid random morphing.
Avoid fantasy imagery.
Avoid excessive slow motion.

Make it PHYSICAL.
Make it LOUD.
Make it UNDERGROUND.

recipe.excerpt: Un cercle orange relie un ballon, une roue, un disque et un œil. Hard Bounce utilise les répétitions de formes et de mouvements dans un clip musical de 24 secondes. Le prompt associe les impacts au son et construit une pause finale.

factors.title: Le repère visuel
factors.body: Répétez un motif reconnaissable. Ici, le cercle orange relie des objets et des lieux différents.

factors.title: Le montage
factors.body: Décrivez le lien vers le plan suivant : un rebond, une rotation similaire ou une forme qui remplit le cadre.

factors.title: La caméra
factors.body: Donnez un point de vue précis à chaque temps : fisheye bas, détail macro ou mouvement rapide en avant. Gardez le mouvement cohérent à la coupe.

factors.title: Le son
factors.body: Associez les impacts physiques au rythme. Précisez la montée du morceau et son arrêt ; cet exemple ne demande aucun dialogue.

section.title: Rendus réels Seedance 2.5
section.intro: Ouvrez un clip pour lire son prompt d’origine et ses réglages. Regardez l’action jusqu’au bout, puis choisissez un élément à changer pour votre propre scène.

proofItems.title: Garder le personnage reconnaissable
proofItems.body: Comparez le visage et les vêtements au début, au milieu et à la fin, surtout quand la personne tourne ou sort du cadre.

proofItems.title: Suivre la caméra
proofItems.body: Observez les changements de cadrage. Pour votre version, essayez de modifier une consigne de caméra en gardant la même action.

proofItems.title: Vérifier les contacts
proofItems.body: Regardez les mains, les pieds et les objets lorsqu’ils se touchent ou bougent. Examinez le contact, pas seulement la première image.

proofItems.title: Écouter aussi
proofItems.body: Pour les exemples sonores, vérifiez si les paroles, l’ambiance et les actions visibles s’accordent.

proofItems.title: Essayer une modification
proofItems.body: Ouvrez le prompt d’origine et les réglages, adaptez un détail, puis vérifiez le nouveau devis avant de générer.

needle vibration,
chrome reflections.

Camera dives INTO the spinning grooves.

--------------------------------
SHOT 5 — 0:07.3–0:09
--------------------------------

The vinyl grooves become curved concrete lines inside a brutalist skate bowl.

A skateboarder drops in at extreme speed.

Wide fisheye lens.

Camera races backward directly in front of the skateboard.

Wheels scream across concrete.

Skater launches over camera.

The underside of the board wipes the entire frame.

WHIP TRANSITION.

--------------------------------
SHOT 6 — 0:09–0:10.7
--------------------------------

Underground rave.

Almost total darkness.

Hard white strobe.

Bodies appear only for fractions of a second.

Sweat.
Chrome jewelry.
Black clothing.
Condensation.
Hands in the air.

In the center:

a giant circular orange speaker cone pulses.

Every bass hit physically moves the cone.

PUSH IN violently on the speaker.

BOOM.

BOOM.

BOOM.

On the third hit—

camera passes through it.

--------------------------------
SHOT 7 — 0:10.7–0:12.3
--------------------------------

Inside a fluorescent laundromat at 2AM.

Perfect symmetrical composition.

Rows of washing machines.

All machine windows are black...

except ONE glowing orange circular door.

Camera crash-zooms toward it.

Inside, orange fabric spins violently.

SPINNING MOTION MATCH CUT.

--------------------------------
SHOT 8 — 0:12.3–0:14
--------------------------------

EXTREME MACRO HUMAN EYE.

The orange washing-machine circle becomes a vivid amber iris.

Natural skin.
Tiny eyelashes.
Wet eye reflections.

The pupil rapidly contracts.

Reflected inside the pupil:

a subway train approaches.

Camera pushes directly through the pupil.

--------------------------------
SHOT 9 — 0:14–0:16
--------------------------------

SUBWAY PLATFORM.

Train blasts past camera at enormous speed.

Handheld.
Harsh fluorescent light.
Wind hits clothing and newspapers.

Very fast cuts:

train wheel —
shoe hitting platform —
door slamming —
hand grabbing metal rail —
orange emergency light —
eyes —
moving tunnel lights.

Each shot lasts only fractions of a second.

CLACK.
CLACK.
CLACK.
CLACK.

The rhythm accelerates.

--------------------------------
SHOT 10 — 0:16–0:18
--------------------------------

CAMERA IS NOW ATTACHED TO THE FRONT OF THE TRAIN.

We rocket through a black subway tunnel.

Circular tunnel lights flash directly toward camera.

Each light appears for one frame:

WHITE.
BLACK.
ORANGE.
BLACK.
WHITE.
BLACK.

Speed increases impossibly.

Then the final tunnel light becomes enormous.

MATCH CUT.

--------------------------------
SHOT 11 — 0:18–0:20
--------------------------------

The circle is now the FULL MOON.

Huge orange moon above brutalist apartment towers.

Camera drops vertically from the moon toward the city at extreme speed.

Down past rooftops,
balconies,
neon,
fire escapes,
streetlights.

FPV dive.

At street level—

someone throws the orange basketball upward directly toward camera.

--------------------------------
SHOT 12 — 0:20–0:22
--------------------------------

BALL FLIES PAST CAMERA.

ULTRA-FAST RHYTHMIC MONTAGE.

0.2–0.4 second fragments:

basketball bounce

motorcycle wheel

vinyl needle

skateboard landing

speaker pumping

washing machine spinning

eye blinking

subway wheel

tunnel light

moon

ball

Every circular image perfectly aligned in the center of frame.

Faster.

Faster.

Faster.

The soundtrack becomes a brutal synchronized audiovisual crescendo.

--------------------------------
SHOT 13 — 0:22–0:24
--------------------------------

Suddenly:

SILENCE.

Back to the exact dark concrete room from the opening.

The fluorescent orange ball drops into frame.

But this time—

a hand catches it ONE CENTIMETER before it hits the ground.

No impact.

Absolute silence.

Hold.

The fingers slowly release the ball.

It begins falling again.

CUT TO BLACK

one frame BEFORE impact.

BOOM.

END.

--------------------------------

AUDIO DESIGN:

Build an original underground electronic track entirely around PHYSICAL IMPACT.

The basketball bounce is the kick drum.

Motorcycle vibration becomes bass texture.

Vinyl crackle becomes high-frequency percussion.

Skateboard wheels become rhythmic noise.

Speaker cone becomes sub-bass.

Subway wheels become industrial percussion.

Train-door impacts become snares.

Tunnel lights introduce sharp electronic pulses.

The track must progressively accelerate from minimal rhythm into an aggressive experimental club beat.

Every important edit must land precisely on sound.

Use aggressive stereo movement during fast camera passages.

At 22 seconds:
REMOVE EVERYTHING.

Absolute silence.

Final BOOM occurs only after picture cuts to black.

--------------------------------

CAMERA LANGUAGE:

extreme fisheye
macro cinematography
camera mounted to moving objects
FPV flight
crash zooms
whip pans
snap zooms
rapid tracking
extreme low angles
Dutch camera rolls
hard handheld
speed ramps
one-frame inserts
perfect graphic match cuts

Avoid generic slow floating AI camera movement.

Camera movement should feel physical, dangerous and intentional.

--------------------------------

VISUAL LANGUAGE:

underground editorial cinema
brutalist architecture
late-night city culture
wet concrete
black asphalt
steel
chrome
sweat
steam
fluorescent practical lights
hard flash photography
16mm texture mixed with sharp modern digital cinematography
deep blacks
controlled highlights
strong grain
dirty lens moments
realistic motion blur

PALETTE:
almost monochrome world,
black,
concrete gray,
cold white,
dirty metallic tones.

FLUORESCENT ORANGE is the only strong recurring color.

Keep orange visually dominant only in the circular motif.

--------------------------------

EDITING RULE:

The audience should constantly anticipate the next impact.

BOUNCE = CUT.
ROTATION = MATCH CUT.
CIRCLE = NEW WORLD.
IMPACT = MUSIC.

Do not create random beautiful shots.

Every shot must visually or rhythmically connect to the previous one.

The video should feel edited by an exceptional human music-video editor:
fast,
precise,
dirty,
cool,
graphic,
unpredictable.

Avoid generic cyberpunk.
Avoid glossy sci-fi.
Avoid random morphing.
Avoid fantasy imagery.
Avoid excessive slow motion.

Make it PHYSICAL.
Make it LOUD.
Make it UNDERGROUND.

shotPlans.prompt: SEEDANCE | TEXT TO VIDEO | SINGLE CONTINUOUS TAKE | 15s | HORIZONTAL 16:9 SCENE AND LOCATION A hidden volcanic spring canyon deep in a Pacific Northwest pine forest on a bright summer day. A narrow deep gorge with high walls of dark gray basalt columns, tan and rust streaks, bright green moss and ferns. At the bottom is a crystal-clear natural spring pool: turquoise shallow edges, deep sapphire center, honeycomb volcanic rock, mossy boulders and two pale submerged logs. Two white waterfalls, one at the far back and one spilling from the right cliff. Tall pine trees line the rim under a clear blue sky. The same canyon layout throughout. THE JUMPER First-person view only. Tanned bare feet, lightly hairy shins and loose navy-blue swim shorts with a mustard-yellow hibiscus pattern. Bare hands and forearms naturally enter frame. No face, shoes or gloves. CAMERA AND REALISM Forehead-mounted action-camera POV with a natural ultra-wide lens. Breathing micro-jitter, head bob, fast exposure shifts between sky and shade, water droplets after immersion, wind buffeting during the fall. Authentic action-camera footage. The drop is about 35 meters. Continuous real-time motion, gravity and water behaviour; keep the same limbs and shorts. 0-2s | THE EDGE AND TAKEOFF Look steeply down at the turquoise pool from the basalt ledge: feet at the bottom of frame and a pink-and-white inflatable tube already floating far below. One sharp breath and a quick "Let's go!" Two quick steps and a decisive push off the edge. The pool and the two waterfalls remain in view as the cliff edge falls away. 2-5s | THE FALL Fast uninterrupted descent. Arms briefly spread at frame edges, then tuck in; legs straighten for a feet-first pencil dive. Basalt and moss rush upward past the lens, right-side waterfall spray catches the sun, wind builds and the camera shakes naturally. The pool and pink tube grow quickly without changing position. One breathless "Wooo!" No pause or slow motion. 5-6s | IMPACT The water fills frame. Feet-first entry: one hard splash, then white bubbles swallow the lens. Audio immediately becomes muffled underwater. 6-10s | UNDERWATER AND ASCENT The bubbles clear into transparent blue water, sun shafts, the same pale logs and basalt bottom. One strong arm pull enters frame, then upward kicks towards the bright surface; bubbles stream past. Keep the ascent fast and purposeful. 10-12s | SURFACE BREAK Burst through the surface. Droplets slide down the lens, wind and waterfall sound return clearly, one hand grabs the pink-and-white tube beside the camera. 12-15s | REWARD Bob on the turquoise water holding the tube. Tilt up to show the towering basalt cliff, the tiny takeoff ledge, pines and right-side waterfall. A real breath, then natural spoken English: "That was insane!" Finish on the cliff view with the water gently bobbing. AUDIO AND CONTINUITY Wind, breathing, waterfall roar, one clear impact splash, bubbles underwater, water movement on resurfacing and the three brief English reactions. One continuous upbeat chill electronic instrumental beneath the real sounds: build through the fall, muffled underwater, then restore clarity with a small beat drop on surfacing. No narration or sung lyrics. One continuous first-person shot, no third-person cut, hovering, extra slow motion, morphing cliffs, changing water colour, extra limbs, titles, subtitles, borders or watermarks.

items.title: Une scène. Une vraie progression.
items.body: Un curseur malicieux transforme une rue ensoleillée en comédie pop : la glace se multiplie, une camionnette change de couleur et un petit chien devient immense. Reliez chaque surprise visuelle à la réaction suivante du personnage.
items.prompt:
30-second live-action POP COMEDY commercial, 16:9, set in present-day Southern California. A mischievous giant DESKTOP MOUSE CURSOR edits the real world around a young woman. Nine short, connected comic beats with a beginning, escalating playful chaos and a cute final punchline. Preserve the playful abundance: ice cream, duplication, a fluffy dog, candy-colored paint, an eraser, a rescue and a surprise hairstyle. Bright, youthful, funny and charming.

LOOK AND PLACE
A sunny Santa Monica neighborhood shopping street: broad American concrete sidewalks, low pastel-pink and mint storefronts, a small ice-cream shop with a striped awning, palm trees, a turquoise bench, a parked compact white delivery van, a coral-brick side alley. Real California street proportions and contemporary American summer styling. Midday sunshine, clear cobalt sky, vivid candy colors, clean whites, crisp faces, colorful details and real tactile materials. Light, buoyant commercial photography with kinetic tracking and comic reaction cuts. No muted sepia palette, brown grading, bleak backstreet or solemn luxury-ad mood. No readable brands or lettering.

CHARACTER CONTINUITY
One fictional 23-year-old woman, called MAYA only for prompt clarity: lively expressive face, shoulder-length dark-brown hair in a high ponytail, small silver hoop earrings, coral-pink fitted short-sleeve T-shirt, white wide-leg jeans, clean white-and-pink sneakers. Natural young-adult American streetwear. Keep her face, body, clothes and accessories identical in every shot. Only her hairstyle changes near the end. She reacts with surprise, mischievous amusement and comic exasperation, never terror.
One small fluffy white bichon with round dark eyes, a tiny pink bandana and a happy wagging tail, initially on a slack coral leash held by a young adult dog walker in a mint sweatshirt. Its later enlarged form is exactly the same adorable dog, with proportional paws and soft detailed curls, never monstrous.

THE CURSOR MUST LOOK LIKE A REAL COMPUTER POINTER
Use the unmistakable classic desktop mouse-pointer silhouette: a broad asymmetric white arrowhead pointing diagonally UPPER LEFT, an inward notch on the lower-right edge and a short diagonal tail. Thin black outline, matte white face, shallow solid thickness. It is NOT an upright street-direction arrow, not a spear, not a signpost. It floats at waist-to-head height, normally about 1.2 meters tall, with accurate shadows, perspective and occlusion in the street. It has an impish personality expressed by quick tilts and bouncy motion, but no face, eyes or limbs.
EVERY click is visible and audible: the pointer tip jabs forward a few centimeters, a crisp mechanical mouse CLICK is clearly heard, and the edit happens immediately in the same shot. A black-and-white dotted selection rectangle and small square transform handles briefly make the operation legible. These are physical graphic shapes embedded in the scene, not a full-screen software interface. For the paint and eraser beats the cursor snaps briefly into those recognizable tool icons, then returns to the same diagonal mouse pointer.

SOUND IS ESSENTIAL
Deliver a clearly audible soundtrack from the first second: original upbeat playful electro-funk/pop instrumental around 116 BPM, bouncy bass, handclaps, tight drums and little sparkling synth accents. Mix sound effects forward so each mouse click and comic action remains unmistakable above the music. Add real footsteps, street ambience, ice-cream pops, a soft elastic enlargement, happy dog barks, paint swoosh, eraser squeaks, rubber-toy squeaks, a splash shake and a final springy BOING. Briefly cut the music before the final hairstyle gag, then bring back a playful ending sting. No dialogue, voice-over, singing or subtitles. Let expressions and synchronized sounds tell the story.

SHOT 1 | 0.0–3.5 s | A DELIGHTFUL LITTLE FAVOR
Medium close shot, slight upward camera tilt following the action. Maya sits on the turquoise bench about to lick a single scoop of strawberry-pink ice cream. Within the first second the classic diagonal mouse cursor swoops into frame and selects the scoop with a tiny dotted rectangle. Four fast visible clicks, each with a distinct CLICK-POP, duplicate the scoop upward into a wobbly five-scoop tower. Each scoop physically rests on the one below. Glossy creamy texture, little melting drips catching the sun. Her eyes follow the growing tower; she breaks into a delighted grin and gives the cursor an appreciative nod. Immediate cute surprise, no static introduction.

SHOT 2 | 3.5–7.0 s | NOW IT GETS CHEEKY
Same bench and screen direction. The cursor pivots toward Maya; CLICK: a dotted rectangle encloses her and the bench. Her grin turns into a suspicious side-eye. Keeping her ice cream upright, she carefully scoots sideways out of the rectangle. CLICK-THUMP: the empty bench duplicates beside the original. The bump makes the upper scoops tumble onto the pavement with soft SPLATS. She looks at her sad remaining scoop, then at the cursor: an unmistakable “really?” look. She leaves the cone on the bench and springs into a playful run toward screen right. Pan with her.

SHOT 3 | 7.0–11.0 s | THE CUTEST ACCIDENT
Lateral tracking shot. Maya nimbly runs around the small bichon and its walker. The cursor's selection misses Maya and lands on the fluffy dog. CLICK: corner handles pull outward, and the dog scales smoothly and proportionally to small-pony size. Elastic BOOP, then one happy low WOOF. Its paws stay grounded; its fur and pink bandana remain identical. The walker lets go of the slack leash in surprised delight, safely staying clear. The giant dog wags its tail enthusiastically and focuses on the cursor as if it were an irresistible toy. Maya does a quick comic double take while continuing right. Make the dog endearing and huggable.

SHOT 4 | 11.0–14.0 s | COLOR FLOOD
Maya ducks alongside the parked white delivery van. The cursor instantly becomes a paint-bucket icon, tips toward the van and CLICKS. A vivid glossy LILAC color races across the van's painted panels with a satisfying liquid SWOOSH. The windows, wheels and headlights remain unchanged. Maya hops clear just before the color reaches where she was leaning, checks her spotless white jeans, gives a tiny relieved smile and keeps moving. Rich purple against pink storefronts and blue sky; clean, instantaneous visual comedy.

SHOT 5 | 14.0–17.5 s | THE ERASER
Tracking alongside the coral-brick wall. The cursor snaps into a chunky white eraser and sweeps toward Maya; she ducks beneath it in one smooth motion. SQUEAK-SQUEAK: the eraser rubs a square of brick into a flat gray-and-white transparency checkerboard, still in perspective on the wall. Maya stops for a fraction of a second, pokes the flat checkerboard with one finger, raises an eyebrow, then darts away as the eraser comes back. The checkerboard is a solid flat surface, not a glowing portal. Keep this curious reaction light and quick.

SHOT 6 | 17.5–22.0 s | THE FLUFFY RESCUE
Maya reaches the end of the colorful side alley and turns. At the entrance, the cursor becomes the diagonal arrow again, briefly scales larger and prepares a selection. Before it can click Maya, the huge happy bichon bounds in from behind it and gently catches the cursor's tail like a rubber dog toy. WOOF, then a clear toy SQUEAK. Cut to a side view of the whole playful action: the dog settles onto its paws, cursor reduced to its usual size, gently chewing it while its tail thumps the sidewalk. Maya exhales and laughs silently with relief. No biting a person, no aggression, no harm.

SHOT 7 | 22.0–25.0 s | FALSE VICTORY
Medium two-shot, warm faces and fluffy texture. Maya scratches the dog's chin, delighted with her rescuer. The dog opens its mouth to pant; the soggy cursor slips onto the pavement. Behind Maya, it bobs back into the air and shakes droplets off with a little PRRR-SPLASH, straightening back into its pristine diagonal pointer shape. She is busy cuddling the dog and does not notice. The audience sees the mischievous comeback.

SHOT 8 | 25.0–27.5 s | ONE LAST CLICK
The music stops for a comic beat. A loud, clean CLICK: a small dotted selection frames ONLY Maya's hair. POP-BOING: her ponytail instantly becomes a huge fluffy BUBBLEGUM-PINK curly hairstyle, a round cloud of springy, individual curls. Keep her exact face, clothing and earrings. She freezes, slowly pats the top of the new hair; it bounces twice with a soft spring sound. Her expression is deadpan disbelief, not distress. The cursor gives an innocent little tilt.

SHOT 9 | 27.5–30.0 s | THE LOOK
Close group composition with the entire pink hairstyle visible, Maya in the middle, the diagonal mouse cursor beside her and the giant bichon's face entering from below. Maya side-eyes the cursor. The adorable dog notices the round bouncy pink hair, tilts its head, wags faster and lowers its front paws into a playful bow. Maya's eyes slide toward the dog: “don't even think about it.” The cursor innocently rocks twice to two little electronic BLIPS. End on this funny three-way reaction with a bright musical button and tail THUMP-THUMP. The dog does not jump on Maya. Hold the expression for the final half-second.

DIRECTING PRIORITIES
Each edit must show target selection, a visible click, a sharp audible click and an immediate result. Keep the cheerful pop energy throughout, with enough reaction time for every joke. Camera tracking carries Maya consistently left to right until the alley; normal clean cuts maintain geography. Physical effects are crisp and harmless, with shadows and material detail. Preserve natural live-action actors and a realistic fluffy dog rather than plastic 3D characters. No text, logos, watermark, unrelated landscape cutaways, beach, doorway or spoken slogan. The final brand title will be added later; generate only the complete colorful comedy with sound.

items.label: Create
items.title: Partez d’une idée. Ou de vos références.
items.body: Décrivez une scène, animez une image de départ ou guidez le résultat avec des images, vidéos et sons de référence. Attribuez un rôle à chaque référence : personnage, mouvement, caméra, décor ou son.
uses: Première + dernière image : guidez le début et la fin d’un plan construit à partir d’images.
Référence de mouvement : reprenez un geste ou un trajet de caméra, puis décrivez le personnage et le décor souhaités.
Multimodal : combinez jusqu’à 30 images, 10 vidéos et 10 références audio.
items.note: De 4 à 30 secondes ou durée automatique, jusqu’en 4K. Les références vidéo partagent 30 secondes ; les références audio disposent de 30 secondes distinctes. Le Draft natif se finalise en 1080p ou 4K.

proof.caption: Exemple illustré : un personnage et un décor réunis dans une scène.
proof.note: Illustration du workflow réalisée avec Sunburst ; la démonstration vidéo Seedance 2.5 reste à rendre. Utilisez cette direction avec vos propres références. Aucun média de référence n’est importé automatiquement.
proof.prompt: Use Image 1 for the fictional adult character and Image 2 for the location. Create a cinematic medium shot of the character walking through the sunlit stone arcade, carrying a paper parcel. Preserve the character’s face, short dark hair and beige coat from Image 1; use the architecture and daylight of Image 2. Track gently beside the character as they look toward the open square, then slow as they stop. Keep the walk readable, with natural fabric movement and consistent screen direction. Sound: footsteps on stone, light city ambience and a soft breeze. No dialogue, music, captions or logos.

items.label: Modify
items.title: Gardez le plan. Changez ce qui compte.
items.body: Importez un clip et décrivez la retouche. Changez un personnage ou sa tenue, remplacez le décor, modifiez la lumière et l’atmosphère, ajoutez ou retirez des éléments. Précisez aussi ce qui doit rester cohérent.
uses: Personnage et style : modifiez l’apparence, les vêtements ou un objet.
Décor et atmosphère : transformez le lieu, la lumière, la météo ou le traitement visuel.
Son et références : guidez les changements audio et illustrez la retouche avec des images, vidéos ou sons.
items.note: Vérifiez les visages, les mains, le mouvement et la continuité après une retouche. Modify standard propose le 480p/720p ; un Draft natif Modify peut être finalisé en 1080p ou en 4K.

proof.caption: Retouche de tenue illustrée · glissez pour comparer tout le cadre.
proof.note: Illustration du workflow réalisée avec Sunburst ; la démonstration vidéo Seedance 2.5 reste à rendre. Utilisez cette direction avec vos propres références. Aucun média de référence n’est importé automatiquement.
proof.prompt: Edit the supplied source video. Change only the ivory coat to deep petrol blue, retaining its cut, fabric texture and movement. Preserve the fictional adult character’s face, hair, black outfit, walking action, camera framing and timing, stone columns, daylight and background. Let the new coat follow the original movement and shadows. Keep the source sound and do not add dialogue, titles or new scene elements. Review face, hands and coat edges throughout the result.

items.label: Extend
items.title: Donnez une suite à la scène.
items.body: Poursuivez après un clip, créez une amorce avant lui ou décrivez une transition entre plusieurs plans. Expliquez l’action au raccord, ainsi que la caméra et le son à prolonger.
uses: Après : terminez une action, révélez le décor ou restez sur une réaction.
Avant : préparez une arrivée ou une amorce avant le plan original.
Entre : utilisez plusieurs clips sources pour guider une transition.
items.note: Jusqu’à 10 clips sources, pour 30 secondes cumulées. Demandez un nouveau segment de 4 à 30 secondes jusqu’en 4K au format de la source, ou explorez un Draft avant son final 1080p/4K. Vérifiez et assemblez la continuation avec vos images.

proof.caption: Suite illustrée · assemblez le nouveau segment avec votre source.
proof.note: Illustration du workflow réalisée avec Sunburst ; la démonstration vidéo Seedance 2.5 reste à rendre. Utilisez cette direction avec vos propres références. Aucun média de référence n’est importé automatiquement.
proof.prompt: Continue after the supplied clip of a skateboarder at a sunlit coastal skatepark. Carry the existing movement into a smooth roll down the transition and toward the open flat. Keep the same character, loose grey shirt, beige trousers, board, daylight, coastal setting and camera direction. Let the camera follow the rider, opening slightly as the action settles. Sound: continuous wheel rumble, a soft concrete scrape and distant sea ambience. No dialogue or music. The first moment of the new segment should connect to the end of the source; do not restart the action.

controls.title: Précisez la réalisation
controls.body: Ajoutez dialogues, ambiance et bruitages, ou désactivez le son généré. Ancrez les détails avec des références image et audio. Choisissez la durée, le format et la résolution dans Create, puis vérifiez le devis avant chaque génération.

models.reason: Travaillez en 480p ou 720p pour essayer une autre prise avant de choisir la version finale.
Préparez un plan de 2 à 30 secondes avec plusieurs types de références, puis retouchez ou prolongez la vidéo.
Composez une séquence de 5 à 15 secondes autour de votre bande-son ou d’un son généré.
